tour.finished: Tour finished — press ? any time for shortcuts
tour.1.title: Everything that is not AI
tour.1.text: This panel drives the deterministic half of ORC — settings, health, runs, knowledge, stats. It never runs a lane and never calls a model. Press 1–9 or 0 to jump between panels; hover here to see the numbers.
tour.2.title: Is anything wrong right now
tour.2.text: Install health, wiki freshness, runs still waiting, and your ORC version with a live update check. If one of these is amber, it is the thing worth reading first.
tour.3.title: One filter over every key
tour.3.text: Filter by key or description across every section at once — you never need to know which tier a key was filed under. 'Changed only' shows just what you have overridden.
tour.4.title: The score → model ladder
tour.4.text: A diagram, not an editor. It comes from the CLI's own table, and it re-draws itself when a setting like opus5_only changes what wins — which is how the precedence rule is taught rather than described.
tour.5.title: Every run ORC recorded
tour.5.text: 'waiting' means a resume pointer is on disk — that run can be picked up in a fresh session. Click one and it opens in place: checkpoint, state of play and trace, without losing the list.
tour.6.title: What ORC already knows
tour.6.text: The wiki, cached code patterns and gotchas. Freshness is computed against the files each doc actually covers, so 'stale' here means something it documents really did change.
tour.7.title: Pick a lane
tour.7.text: Copy any lane command, or open a Claude session in this repo. The panel hands off to a terminal and forgets — nothing about that session comes back here.
tour.8.title: Preview, then apply
tour.8.text: Nothing here runs on its own. Every action shows the CLI's own read-only preview first and the exact command it will run — and a prune names every file, because a count is not consent.
tour.upgrade.title: Upgrade is here
tour.upgrade.text: Click Preview… to see exactly what it would install and run. Nothing happens until you approve it.
tour.9.title: The promises
tour.9.text: These are the rules your project promised to follow. ORC checks them for you and tells you which ones the code has moved under.
tour.10.title: Where ORC stops
tour.10.text: This is work ORC will not do on its own yet. The checklist says exactly what would change that - and you can always tell it to go ahead anyway.
tour.11.title: Things you can change yourself
tour.11.text: No code, no terminal. A check runs afterwards, and the undo command is shown before anything is written.
tour.12.title: The cheap part of the wiki
tour.12.text: Refreshing the whole wiki is expensive. This is the short, ranked list that actually matters - and the free repairs always come first.
tour.13.title: A long document, in one picture
tour.13.text: Each block is a section, sized by how long it is and coloured by its state. Nothing here loads the document itself - ORC works from this map instead, which is why a long document does not end the session.
tour.14.title: Work that runs somewhere else
tour.14.text: One line from nothing to a hundred: how hard a task scored. Every part of it shows where that work actually runs — Claude in blue, a provider you connected in green. A range you have not connected keeps its slot, so "I left the hard work on Claude on purpose" never looks like "there is no hard work". Nothing leaves this machine until you connect something, test it, and press Apply.
